NoteNlpAccessor::remove_headers¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteNlpAccessor::remove_headers() const

Remove Hash-Marked Heading Lines¶

remove_headers() removes complete hash-marked heading lines from each text cell. It is intended for extracted or authored text in which headings are structural labels and the body is the material to retain. The complete line is deleted; this is not a marker-stripping operation that turns ## Results into Results.

After optional leading spaces or tabs, a heading must satisfy both conditions:

Component

Rule

Marker count

Between one and six consecutive # bytes

Marker boundary

End of line, a space, or a tab immediately after the final #

Consequently, # Title,    ### Results, and a line containing only ## are headings. ####### Seven is retained because seven markers are outside the supported level range. #include <vector> and #topic are retained because the marker is immediately followed by a non-whitespace byte. Those distinctions let source fragments and hashtag-like prose coexist with heading cleanup without being silently discarded.

When at least one heading is removed, surviving lines are joined through collapsed ASCII whitespace and stripped. This produces compact prose from a multi-section cell. When no heading exists, the original bytes are returned exactly, including line breaks and indentation. If every line is a heading, the corresponding result cell is empty rather than absent.

The method allocates a new shape-identical Text Note and does not mutate the receiver. Every cell is classified independently. Undefined and empty Notes propagate according to the common Note transform contract; Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes reject because line classification is defined only for Text. Cells without # bypass line parsing entirely.

Example 1: Heading Levels And Indentation¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({
        "# Heading\nBody\n   ### Nested\nText\n"
        "####### Seven\n#include <x>\n#topic"})
        .nlp().remove_headers()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Body Text ####### Seven #include <x> #topic"]

Only the one- and three-marker heading lines are removed. The seven-marker, preprocessor-like, and tag-like lines become part of the compacted body.

Example 2: Hash-Prefixed Non-Headings Are Exact No-Ops¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"  #topic\n#include <vector>  "})
        .nlp().remove_headers()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["  #topic\n#include <vector>  "]

Because neither line has whitespace after a valid marker run, no transformation occurs and the cell’s formatting remains untouched.

Example 3: Classification Is Per Cell¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a@b.io", "Page 1", "#tag", "<b>bold</b>"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.nlp().remove_headers()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a@b.io", "Page 1"], 
  ["#tag", "<b>bold</b>"]
]

#tag is not a heading, and the matrix’s two-dimensional shape is retained.
